classification.difficultyReason: Part b requires recognising equal radii and vertically opposite central angles to match the triangles, then linking isosceles base angles, the triangle angle sum and corresponding angles. Congruence is supplied, so the work is a routine chain of deductions rather than discovering a proof strategy.

content.prompt: Each pair of triangles is congruent. Name the two triangles with the vertices in the correct order and then find the value of each pronumeral.

spec.description: Two intersecting triangles with central vertex L; one, two and three side ticks identify corresponding sides. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: A,L,N are collinear; T,L,M are collinear. AL=LN, TL=LM, AT=MN. Angle TAL=61 degrees; angle LMN=52 degrees. Unknowns are LTA=alpha, ALT=beta and LNM=gamma.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angles and unknown labels are visible.

answer.worked:
$AL=NL$, $LT=LM$ and $AT=NM$ (matching side marks), so $\triangle ALT\equiv\triangle NLM$ (SSS).

$\alpha=52^\circ$ and $\gamma=61^\circ$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).

By the angle sum of $\triangle ALT$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-61^\circ-52^\circ\\\beta&=67^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: ($O$ is the centre of the circle.)

spec.description: Circle with intersecting diameters PR and QS, chords PS and QR, centre O and its red point. Ordinary outlines and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: PR and QS are diameters. Angle QOR=106 degrees, POS=gamma, SPR=beta and PRQ=theta.
spec.answerVisibility: The given central angle and unknown labels are visible; calculated angles remain hidden.

answer.short:
$\triangle POS\equiv\triangle ROQ$ (SAS); $\gamma=106^\circ$, $\beta=37^\circ$, $\theta=37^\circ$.

Use equal radii, vertically opposite angles and the base angles of isosceles triangles.
answer.worked:
$\gamma=106^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).

In $\triangle POS$ and $\triangle ROQ$, $OP=OR$ and $OS=OQ$ (radii), and $\angle POS=\angle ROQ$ (vertically opposite angles). Hence $\triangle POS\equiv\triangle ROQ$ (SAS).

Since $OP=OS$, $\triangle POS$ is isosceles. Its base angles are equal, so
$$\begin{align*}2\beta+106^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\beta&=74^\circ\\\beta&=37^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Matching angles of the congruent triangles give $\theta=\beta=37^\circ$.
